one_line_input: a product shot of the quiet-desk switch set and desk mat combo on a measurement rig
big_idea: The switches and mat aren't styled, they're under test — the rig is the proof, not a prop.
visual_description: Top-down, instrument-angle shot of a bench-style acoustic measurement rig on a plain matte grey surface. The quarterly switch set sits in an open tray or fanned row at the center of the rig, with the desk mat positioned flat beneath or beside it as the test substrate. A steel ruler or calibration scale runs along one edge of the frame for size reference. A small boom-mounted microphone or dB meter is positioned near the switches, its display showing a legible measured reading (e.g. '38 dB'). Lighting is even, cool, and directional like a lab photo — no warm ambient glow, no bokeh, no soft shadows.
style_notes: Reads like a page from an acoustic test report, not a product catalog or desk-aesthetic flat-lay. Matte black and neutral grey dominate, with a single calibration-yellow or safety-orange accent (a clamp, a cable, a meter housing) as the only color note. Monospace or technical grotesk if any incidental labels/markings appear on the rig itself. Clinical, quiet confidence — the measurement does the talking, nothing is styled to look aspirational.
must_preserve: the switch set and desk mat remain the visual anchor of the frame, not the rig hardware itself
the meter/display on the rig shows a legible, plausible measured reading, treated as a real diegetic instrument reading, not a graphic overlay
top-down or instrument-angle framing with a visible ruler or scale reference for size/scale credibility
palette stays restricted to matte black, neutral greys, and one calibration accent color — no RGB gradients

stays within the established visual pillars: product photography as measurement subject on a rig, dashboard/data-sheet visual language, dB figures shown in typographic or instrument-display focus rather than adjectives
forbidden: no glossy RGB lighting, gamer aesthetic, or 'unleash/dominate' visual energy
no lifestyle desk flat-lay staging — no plants, coffee cups, warm window light, or aspirational styling
no unquantified 'quiet' or 'silent' claim rendered anywhere with no accompanying number
no soft rounded card framing, Instagram-square mood-board collage, or pastel/beige lifestyle tones
no visible DIY lubing tools or implication the customer needs to lube the switches themselves
